sections.html:
A Jacksonville owner can accept a cash offer, list with an agent, or sell a rental with the tenants still living in it. Investor interest is strong here because fewer than four in ten homes are lived in by their owners.

The city sits on the New River in Onslow County. Renters and service families shape demand, and an investor planning to rent will price a house differently from a family planning to move in. Decide which buyer you are really talking to before you set expectations on price.

sections.h2: How the Jacksonville market differs from a suburb
sections.html:
Jacksonville has more renters than owners, a midpoint owner-held home value near $210,000, and a population that has barely moved since 2020. The 2025 estimate is 72,732, against 72,723 counted in 2020. Owners live in 38.7% of homes, midpoint rent is $1,321 a month, and midpoint household income is $57,697.

Turnover is brisk, with only 72.1% of residents at the same address for a full year. The average trip to work is a short 15.0 minutes. Demand leans toward rentals and starter houses, and with a small share of older residents, fewer sellers rely on age-based tax relief. The disabled veteran exclusion has no age limit, so it still comes up.

Price a house against nearby sales of similar size, age and condition, not against the statewide picture. The city website posts current planning projects if a buyer asks about the area.

sections.h2: Preparing for an investor or cash buyer
sections.html:
Rental investors and cash buyers buy paperwork as much as buildings, so gather it first.

  • A copy of the deed and your most recent tax bill from the Onslow County Tax Office.
  • Lease agreements, rent ledgers and deposit records for any tenant in the house.
  • Receipts for roof, heating and cooling, plumbing and electrical work.
  • Payoff letters for each loan or lien.

The county's revaluation took effect January 1, 2026, so your assessed value reflects that date. The online property search shows what the tax office has on file. Look for errors in square footage or features and report any mistakes to the tax office, so your numbers match what you tell a buyer.

Each route suits a different seller.

  • Cash offer. Suits owners who must move quickly or skip repairs, and investors who plan to rent.
  • Agent listing. Works for well-kept houses, with owner-held homes at a $210,100 midpoint.
  • Sale with tenants in place. Appeals to investors who want existing rent, and requires a lease and rent history.
  • Pre-listing repairs. Worth it only if the work adds more than it costs, so get quotes first.

For a vacant house after a move, set the monthly cost of carrying it against a discounted quick sale. The loan, insurance, tax and upkeep run every month it sits empty.

Onslow County revalued all real property as of January 1, 2026, and the next revaluation is scheduled for January 1, 2030.

The tax office runs a four-year cycle, though state law allows eight years. It prices property by mass appraisal, drawing on recent sales, building permits, computer modeling, aerial imagery and some field visits, and not every parcel is inspected. The county points out that revaluation does not itself raise taxes, because the commissioners set the rate separately in the budget.

  • Filing an appeal costs nothing, and no attorney or formal appraisal is required.
  • Useful evidence includes comparable sales from before January 1, 2026 and photographs.
  • An independent board appointed by the commissioners hears appeals, and you may skip the hearing.
  • The tax office answers questions at 910-989-2200.

The county's revaluation FAQ also explains how to correct wrong square footage or features. Call the tax office for the current appeal deadline on your parcel.

sections.h2: Closing costs and tax items for a seller
sections.html:
The seller owes the state stamp tax and any unpaid property tax, plus the loan payoff and agent or buyer fees.

The Onslow County registry takes the stamp, at a dollar per $500 of price or part of $500, ahead of recording. Its fees begin at $26 for a general instrument and $64 for a mortgage deed. G.S. 47-18 protects the buyer against later claims only after registration.

Real estate tax is a lien from the listing date, so get the proration figure from the tax office. Exemptions cut taxable value, and a buyer who expects one, such as the disabled veteran exclusion, must apply to the county.

sections.h2: Selling a Jacksonville rental with tenants
sections.html:
A sale does not end a lease, so the buyer normally inherits it. If you need the house empty, G.S. 42-14 sets the notice by tenancy type. A tenant who has not paid within 10 days of demand risks forfeiting the lease, and the case goes to a magistrate in small claims court.

Small claims eviction costs and timing
StepAmount or timing
Filing fee$96

Typical hearing date10 to 15 days out

Dates and fees come from the court system's own guide, so confirm them with the clerk before you file. Many buyers would rather inherit a paying tenant than wait on a court date.

sections.h2: If you are behind on a Jacksonville mortgage
sections.html:
A clerk's hearing comes before any power-of-sale foreclosure.

The lender must serve notice ahead of the hearing, and a reported sale stays open to higher bids for a short time. With homes valued near $210,100, equity may be thin, so a payoff figure matters. Ask your servicer for it, then compare a sale before the hearing with the cost of waiting.

If the numbers look tight, bring your payoff letter, tax bill and any offers to a housing counselor or attorney before you commit to a buyer.

1. Pull together the deed, tax bill, leases and repair receipts.
  2. Collect written offers and ask each buyer for a net proceeds figure.
  3. The closing attorney searches title and requests payoff letters.
  4. You review the settlement statement and sign. The deed goes to the Onslow County registry for filing.

A cash buyer skips loan approval, so the schedule is mostly title work. Settle the move-out date, who keeps the keys and how tenants, if any, will be told before closing.

faqs.a: Barely. The 2025 estimate of 72,732 compares with 72,723 counted in 2020, a change of 0.1%.

faqs.q: When will Onslow County revalue again?
faqs.a: The tax office schedules the next one for January 1, 2030. The current schedule of values began January 1, 2026.

faqs.q: Does an Onslow County appeal cost money?
faqs.a: No. The county charges no fee and does not require an attorney or a formal appraisal.

faqs.q: Who pays the state stamp on a Jacksonville deed?
faqs.a: The seller pays it to the Onslow County registry before the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Can a Jacksonville house sell with tenants?
faqs.a: Yes. Give the buyer the lease and payment history. If you need the house vacant, follow G.S. 42-14 and the small claims process.
